stages.name: Protectionism and the trade balance
stages.title: Protectionism and the trade balance
stages.sub: How shielding home industries from foreign competition changes a country's net trade position.

steps.q: A government puts an extra charge on every washing machine imported from abroad, making them more expensive in shops. What is this extra charge designed to do to imported goods?
steps.right: Make them more expensive than home-made ones
steps.wrong: Make them cheaper than home-made ones
steps.hint: Think about why the government would add this charge to something coming from abroad.

steps.q: Instead of a charge, the government simply says only 1,000 foreign cars can be sold this year, no matter how many people want to buy them. What happens to the number of foreign cars sold beyond that limit?
steps.right: None more can be sold, whatever the demand
steps.wrong: More can still be sold if demand is high enough
steps.hint: The government has fixed a maximum number, not a price.
steps.pre: This limit on the physical amount of a good that can be imported is an import

steps.q: Tariffs and quotas both make it harder or more expensive for foreign firms to sell into a country. What is a government doing to the market when it uses tools like these?
steps.right: Deliberately shielding home firms from foreign competition
steps.hint: Both tools work against foreign sellers and in favour of domestic ones.
